publish.reason: Character frames live under players/, mobs/ and bosses/ but are packed as characters/…; the promotion bridge needs the frame key to equal the processed path, and character atlases carry no per-frame pivot yet. Edit, review and restore work; publishing is not wired.
Their keys equal the atlas keys, but promotion into the atlases has only been verified for UI and VFX frames. Enable it here once a promotion test passes for the category.
Icons live under icons/ but are packed with the UI group (ui/…), so the frame key differs from the processed path the promotion bridge requires.
Longtime assets are packed into per-chunk atlases by the Longtime QA packer (qa_longtime.py), which does not read approved frames.

rules: Perspective: 3/4 top-down dungeon view (Soul Knight style). Characters face the viewer; walls are 2.5D (front face plus top cap); floors are flat top faces. No side view, no 2:1 isometric diamond.
Outline: 1 px solid ink_01 (#14101a) on the outer silhouette of every sprite; alpha is binary (0 or 255), and fully transparent pixels carry RGB 0,0,0.

Palette: exactly the 40 colours in studio_project_info, nothing else; take hex values from there, never invent one. Light comes from the top left and shade ramps run dark to light inside one colour group.
Grid: native pixel art at the size class of the asset (character 32x32, boss 64 to 96 square, tile 16x16, icon 16 or 24); enlarge only by whole-number nearest-neighbour scaling.
Characters are sturdy and large-headed, not realistic: studio_template_get returns this project's proportions; accent colours need bold patches.
Locomotion comes from drawn key poses on a pose sheet, idle and small motions from a rig, asymmetric marks from stored pixel patches (studio_frame_patch), never from redrawing.
Environment, items, projectiles and VFX are code-drawn (studio_generator_run, studio_vfx_build); an image tool draws characters, mobs and bosses only.
Nothing you call approves art or signs audio listening: a human does, in the review tabs. A different session than the author makes the independent check.

prompt.style: Chunky pixel-art-ready character art: flat colour clusters, clear contours, crisp cel shading, no realism, no texture, no thin lines, no busy highlights; every colour must be one of the project's 40 palette colours.

kiln_keeper.description: Elderly xianxia kiln keeper, a small human in a plain grey-blue robe, one leather apron strapped over the character's RIGHT shoulder only (asymmetric), holding a very long iron tongs in the RIGHT hand extending down and forward, bald head with a small grey topknot, soot-smudged, calm face.

ink_marten.description: Small ink marten, a slender weasel-like animal standing on all four legs, glossy dark ink-black fur, a very long thick ink-black tail trailing behind it, cream-white muzzle and chest. Large upright rounded ears. The LEFT ear has a bright cream-white triangular notch cut out of its tip, clearly visible as a pale gap; the RIGHT ear is solid dark and whole.

humanoid.description: Upright characters with a head, a torso and two legs: the shipped players, and humanoid mobs and NPCs. Head share is head height over figure height; every length of the guide is a fraction of the figure height.
humanoid.measured: six shipped 32x32 humanoids (wl_blood_foundation, wl_extreme_jing, wl_outer_disciple, wl_qi_condensation, mob_courtyard_guard, mob_rogue_disciple), idle and walk frames facing south in assets/processed, measured with studio/forge/figure measureFigure: head share (head height over figure height, where a neck shows) 0.31 to 0.38 for nine of eleven frames, one frame 0.50 and one 0.11 (a hat), median 0.37; leg width in the bottom rows (median run of opaque pixels) 4 to 9 px, never below 4; widest row 0.52 to 0.69 of the height; accent colours 5 to 20 px per palette id (blood, bronze, jade). The minimum limb width is set one pixel under the thinnest shipped figure.

primitives.description: Primitive sprites on the project palette: diamond, disc, ring, cross, star, drop or shard, outlined, one or more pulsing frames. Writes <clip>_<direction>_<n>.png.
